/-!
# BV prime-window sources as co-Poisson normal classes

This file records the algebraic connection behind the pole-cancelled BV source.

For a principal multiplier ideal `I = (Λ)`, differentiation does not generally
descend to `A / I`: its failure to preserve `I` is precisely the transverse
class

`Λ g ↦ [D Λ · g] ∈ A / I`.

The induced map on `I` kills `I²`, so it is a conormal map.  For the completed
zeta multiplier, the pole-cancelled BV source is the sum of a multiple of `Λ`
and this normal class.  On a zero fibre, only the normal class survives.

These statements are algebraic/analytic connection laws.  They do not assert
the Hilbert-space sign or contraction needed by the terminal RH criterion.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Set Topology

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

variable {R A : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]

/-- Principal source ideal generated by the completed multiplier. -/
def principalSourceIdeal (Λ : A) : Ideal A := Ideal.span {Λ}

/--
Normal derivative of a principal source ideal.

The Leibniz defect that would obstruct `D` from descending to the quotient
vanishes because its coefficient lies in the principal ideal.
-/
def principalSourceNormalDerivative
    (D : Derivation R A A) (Λ : A) :
    principalSourceIdeal Λ →ₗ[A] A ⧸ principalSourceIdeal Λ where
  toFun x := Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D x.1)
  map_add' x y := by
    simp only [Submodule.coe_add, map_add]
  map_smul' a x := by
    change Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D (a * x.1)) =
      a • Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D x.1)
    rw [D.leibniz]
    change Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (a * D x.1 + x.1 * D a) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (a * D x.1)
    simp only [map_add, map_mul]
    have hx : Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) x.1 = 0 :=
      Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr x.2
    rw [hx, zero_mul, add_zero]

/-- On a generator multiple, the normal derivative is `[D Λ · g]`. -/
theorem principalSourceNormalDerivative_generator_mul
    (D : Derivation R A A) (Λ g : A) :
    principalSourceNormalDerivative D Λ
        ⟨Λ * g, (principalSourceIdeal Λ).mul_mem_right g
          (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton Λ))⟩ =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D Λ * g) := by
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D (Λ * g)) =
    Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D Λ * g)
  rw [D.leibniz]
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (Λ * D g + g * D Λ) =
    Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D Λ * g)
  simp only [map_add, map_mul]
  have hΛ : Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) Λ = 0 :=
    Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr
      (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton Λ))
  rw [hΛ, zero_mul, zero_add]
  exact mul_comm _ _

/-- The normal derivative kills products of two source-ideal elements. -/
theorem principalSourceNormalDerivative_mul_eq_zero
    (D : Derivation R A A) (Λ : A)
    (x y : principalSourceIdeal Λ) :
    principalSourceNormalDerivative D Λ
        ⟨x.1 * y.1, (principalSourceIdeal Λ).mul_mem_left x.1 y.2⟩ = 0 := by
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (principalSourceIdeal Λ) (D (x.1 * y.1)) = 0
  rw [D.leibniz]
  apply Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr
  exact (principalSourceIdeal Λ).add_mem
    ((principalSourceIdeal Λ).mul_mem_right (D y.1) x.2)
    ((principalSourceIdeal Λ).mul_mem_right (D x.1) y.2)

The two bonding maps `T_j^+ = E_j U_r^*` and `T_j^- = E_j U_r` are exchanged by the cosine
involution, and on the co-Poisson annihilator boundary they act on the quotient kernel by the two
reciprocal characters.  Two consequences are recorded here.

* The two-path commutator applied to a quotient kernel is exactly the source-error expression: the
  characters cancel and what remains is the image of the co-Poisson source defects at the two
  levels above.  On the annihilator boundary the defects vanish, so the commutator does.

  aperture-kernel norm.  A rank-one reciprocal system with that flatness has exactly one gauge

/-- The composite of a finite word in the two bonding maps, read from the left. -/
def coPoissonWordOp (a r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) :
    List Bool → ℕ → (evenSubspace →L[ℂ] evenSubspace)
  | [], j => burnolCoPoissonQuotientProjection (soninAperture a r j) (soninAperture_pos ha hr j)
  | (b :: ε), j =>
      (if b then coPoissonQuotientForward a r ha hr j
        else coPoissonQuotientInverse a r ha hr j).comp
        (coPoissonWordOp a r ha hr ε (j + 1))

theorem coPoissonWordOp_apply_mem (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) (ε : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (x : evenSubspace) :
    coPoissonWordOp a r ha hr ε j x ∈ burnolCoPoissonQuotientSpace (soninAperture a r j) := by
  cases ε with
  | nil => exact burnolCoPoissonQuotientProjection_apply_mem _ (soninAperture_pos ha hr j) _
  | cons b ε =>
      rw [coPoissonWordOp, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]
      by_cases hb : b
      · simp only [hb, if_pos]
        exact coPoissonQuotientForward_apply_mem a r ha hr j _
      · simp only [hb, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
        exact coPoissonQuotientInverse_apply_mem a r ha hr j _

theorem norm_coPoissonWordOp_apply_le (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) (ε : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (x : evenSubspace) : ‖coPoissonWordOp a r ha hr ε j x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ := by
  induction ε generalizing j with
  | nil =>
      letI : CompleteSpace (burnolCoPoissonQuotientSpace (soninAperture a r j)) :=
        (isClosed_burnolCoPoissonQuotientSpace (soninAperture_pos ha hr j)).completeSpace_coe
      exact (burnolCoPoissonQuotientSpace (soninAperture a r j)).norm_starProjection_apply_le x
  | cons b ε ih =>
      rw [coPoissonWordOp, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]
      by_cases hb : b
      · simp only [hb, if_pos]
        exact le_trans (norm_coPoissonQuotientForward_apply_le a r ha hr j _) (ih (j + 1))

/-!
# Explicit separated source-packet reconstruction of Hurwitz orientation

The abstract continued-Cauchy closure of the canonical Xi--Hurwitz orientation vector can be
realized by actual finite packets on which every pairwise prime--Gamma divided difference is
defined.  Pairwise-separated packets are dense in each algebraic packet, hence their evaluations
have the same Hilbert closure as the continued Cauchy algebraic core.

There is therefore an unconditional sequence of finite, pairwise-separated continued-source
packets whose evaluation vectors converge to the orientation vector and whose explicit
prime--Gamma energies converge to `-xiHurwitzOrientationEnergy`.

This closes the analytic packet-representation and collision layer.  It does not close RH: the
sequence is extracted through the target orientation closure, so the remaining theorem must either
select it from source values alone or prove its eventual source sign independently.
-/

/-- A finite continued-source Cauchy packet with every pairwise conjugate denominator separated. -/
structure XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket where
  index : Type
  fintypeIndex : Fintype index
  coeff : index → ℂ
  pole : index → XiContinuedCauchyPoint
  separated : ∀ i j, (pole i : ℂ) ≠ (starRingEnd ℂ) (pole j : ℂ)

def XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket.evaluation
    (P : XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket) :
    lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2 := by
  letI := P.fintypeIndex
  exact xiWeilContinuedCauchyPacketLp P.coeff P.pole

def XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket.sourceEnergy
    (P : XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket) : ℝ := by
  letI := P.fintypeIndex
  exact continuedCauchyPacketSourceEnergy P.coeff P.pole

/-- A separated packet's explicit source energy equals its unconditional Xi Weil Hilbert value. -/
theorem XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket.sourceEnergy_eq_hilbertQuadratic
    (P : XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket) :
    P.sourceEnergy = xiWeilHilbertQuadratic P.evaluation := by
  letI := P.fintypeIndex
  exact (xiWeilHilbertQuadratic_indexedCauchyPacket_eq_continuedSource_re
    P.coeff P.pole P.separated).symm

def xiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacketEvaluationSet :
    Set (lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) :=
  Set.range XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket.evaluation

/-- Every algebraic continued Cauchy vector lies in the Hilbert closure of actual separated
packet evaluations. -/
theorem continuedCauchyAlgebraicSubspace_le_closure_separatedPacketEvaluations :
    (xiWeilContinuedCauchyAlgebraicSubspace :
      Set (lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2)) ⊆
      closure xiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacketEvaluationSet := by
  intro v hv
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_finsupp_indexedCauchyPacket_eq_of_mem v hv
  let ι := {x // x ∈ c.support}
  let coeff : ι → ℂ := fun i => c i.1
  let pole : ι → XiContinuedCauchyPoint := fun i => i.1
  obtain ⟨w, hwsep, hw, _henergy⟩ :=
    exists_pairwiseConjSeparatedContinuedSourceEnergy_tendsto coeff pole
  let P : ℕ → XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket := fun n =>
    { index := ι
      fintypeIndex := inferInstance
      coeff := coeff
      pole := w n
      separated := hwsep n }
  have hP : Tendsto (fun n => (P n).evaluation) atTop (nhds v) := by
    change Tendsto (fun n => xiWeilContinuedCauchyPacketLp coeff (w n))
      atTop (nhds v)
    rw [← hc]
    exact hw
  exact mem_closure_of_tendsto hP
    (Eventually.of_forall fun n => ⟨P n, rfl⟩)

/-- The canonical orientation vector belongs to the closure of evaluations of explicit finite
pairwise-separated continued-source packets. -/
theorem xiHurwitzOrientationVector_mem_closure_separatedPacketEvaluations :
    xiHurwitzOrientationVector ∈
      closure xiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacketEvaluationSet := by
  have hclosure : closure
      (xiWeilContinuedCauchyAlgebraicSubspace :
        Set (lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2)) ⊆
      closure xiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacketEvaluationSet :=
    closure_minimal
      continuedCauchyAlgebraicSubspace_le_closure_separatedPacketEvaluations
      isClosed_closure
  exact hclosure xiHurwitzOrientationVector_mem_continuedCauchyHilbertSubspace

/-- An unconditional sequence of explicit separated packets converges to the canonical
orientation vector. -/
theorem exists_separatedContinuedCauchyPackets_tendsto_orientationVector :
    ∃ P : ℕ → XiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacket,
      Tendsto (fun n => (P n).evaluation) atTop
        (nhds xiHurwitzOrientationVector) := by
  have hclosure :=
    xiHurwitzOrientationVector_mem_closure_separatedPacketEvaluations
  have happ : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ v,
      v ∈ xiSeparatedContinuedCauchyPacketEvaluationSet ∧
      dist xiHurwitzOrientationVector v < 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1) := by
    intro n
    exact Metric.mem_closure_iff.mp hclosure _ (by positivity)

/-!
# Source-pointed strict descent law

Exact range realization and approximation are different transport invariants.  A continuous
consumer sends an approximable source value to an approximable output value.  If that consumer is
also injective, it reflects exact range membership.  Consequently a point in `closure(range) \
range` stays in `closure(range) \ range` after every continuous injective downstream consumer.

This is the topological irreversibility law complementary to kernel-pair monotonicity.  An
injective consumer can retain a closure-only boundary value, but it cannot manufacture the source
primitive that failed to exist upstream.
-/

/-- An injective downstream consumer reflects exact membership in the upstream range. -/
theorem mem_range_comp_iff_of_injective
    {X Y Z : Type*} (T : X → Y) (J : Y → Z)
    (hJ : Function.Injective J) (y : Y) :
    J y ∈ Set.range (J ∘ T) ↔ y ∈ Set.range T := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    refine ⟨x, hJ ?_⟩
    simpa only [Function.comp_apply] using hx
  · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨x, rfl⟩

/-- A continuous downstream consumer preserves closure admission of an upstream range value. -/
theorem mem_closure_range_comp_of_continuous
    {X Y Z : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace Z]
    (T : X → Y) (J : Y → Z) (hJ : Continuous J) {y : Y}
    (hy : y ∈ closure (Set.range T)) :
    J y ∈ closure (Set.range (J ∘ T)) := by
  have himage : J y ∈ closure (J '' Set.range T) := by
    apply image_closure_subset_closure_image hJ
    exact ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
  have hrange : J '' Set.range T = Set.range (J ∘ T) := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, ⟨x, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨x, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨T x, ⟨x, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
  rwa [hrange] at himage

/-- **Closure-only persistence.**  Continuous injective postprocessing preserves exact
nonattainment as well as approximation. -/
theorem continuous_injective_consumer_preserves_closureOnly
    {X Y Z : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace Z]
    (T : X → Y) (J : Y → Z) (hJcont : Continuous J)
    (hJinj : Function.Injective J) {y : Y}
    (hyClosure : y ∈ closure (Set.range T))
    (hyNotRange : y ∉ Set.range T) :
    J y ∈ closure (Set.range (J ∘ T)) ∧
      J y ∉ Set.range (J ∘ T) := by
  refine ⟨mem_closure_range_comp_of_continuous T J hJcont hyClosure, ?_⟩
  rwa [mem_range_comp_iff_of_injective T J hJinj y]

/-- A law imposed on every primitive of a surjective transport is already a law on the whole
target.  Surjective strictification therefore cannot select a proper purity locus without an
additional source-sector restriction. -/
theorem target_law_of_forall_source_of_surjective
    {X Y : Type*} (T : X → Y) (hT : Function.Surjective T)
    (P : Y → Prop) (hP : ∀ x : X, P (T x)) :
    ∀ y : Y, P y := by
  intro y
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := hT y
  exact hP x

/-- Contrapositive selection form: if a target property fails somewhere, every surjective
transport has a source primitive on which it fails. -/
theorem exists_source_not_target_law_of_surjective
    {X Y : Type*} (T : X → Y) (hT : Function.Surjective T)
    (P : Y → Prop) (hP : ∃ y : Y, ¬ P y) :
    ∃ x : X, ¬ P (T x) := by
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hP
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := hT y
  exact ⟨x, hy⟩

theorem differentialMatroid_closure_eq_differentialClosure

    [Differential F] [Differential E] [DifferentialAlgebra F E] [CharZero E]
    {G H : Set E} (hGH : G ⊆ H) :
